command: python3 evals/gene-identity/gic_benchmark.py --variant quote-title -j 6 --note first run, L2

record.name: D1
record.evidence: "We here study dopaminoceptive neurons in mouse ventral hippocampus (vHipp), molecularly distinguished by their expression of dopamine D1 or D2 receptors"
record.rationale: Looking up "D1" as written gave UNIQUE_SYNONYM → Dio1 (iodothyronine deiodinase 1), which does not fit: the evidence is about dopamine receptor-expressing neurons. The quote says "dopamine D1 or D2 receptors", and D1 is the standard neuroscience abbreviation for the dopamine D1 receptor, encoded by Drd1. I looked up Drd1 in mouse and got EXACT_SYMBOL → NCBIGene:13488. The quote names the receptor in words but does not give the gene symbol, so the Drd1 mapping rests on the field's convention.

record.name: D1
record.evidence: "In the vCA1 pyramidal cell layer, gradual enrichment of both D1 and D2 cells emerges ventral to the rhinal fissure, along with the diffuse 21 transition from vCA1 to vSub."
record.rationale: Looking up 'D1' as written gave UNIQUE_SYNONYM -> Dio1 (deiodinase 1). That does not fit: the paper is about dopaminoceptive D1 and D2 neurons in ventral hippocampus, and its quote does not define D1. In dopamine neuroscience, D1 and D2 are the standard abbreviations for the D1 and D2 dopamine receptors. D1 therefore means dopamine receptor D1, whose mouse gene is Drd1. This rests on field convention, not on a definition in the quote. The gene ID and symbol come from the lookup of 'Drd1' (EXACT_SYMBOL -> NCBIGene:13488). The 'D1 cells' are neurons expressing this receptor. The paper's title supplied context only.

record.name: D2
record.evidence: "We used two mouse lines that allow for Cre‐dependent viral labeling of MCs and their axons: dopamine receptor D2 (Drd2‐Cre) and calcitonin receptor‐like receptor (Crlr‐Cre)." (PMID:33600026)
record.rationale: The lookup of the bare string 'D2' returned only UNIQUE_SYNONYM Slc3a1 (NCBIGene:20532). That gene does not fit the evidence, so I rejected it. The paper defines D2 as dopamine receptor D2 and names the Drd2-Cre line used to label mossy cells. I looked up Drd2 instead. It returned EXACT_SYMBOL, Drd2 (NCBIGene:13489), mouse. The lookup used the pinned gene-id build, because GENE_ID_BIN was not set.

record.name: SP
record.evidence: "labels a sparse number of INs located mainly within the SO and SP layers of CA1-CA3"
record.rationale: In this hippocampal context SP is the stratum pyramidale layer, listed alongside SO (stratum oriens) and the subregions CA1-CA3. It is not a gene product, and it does not mean substance P (Tac1). No gene lookup was run, because only GENE names go through the lookup steps. The identification rests on the quote and on hippocampal layer naming conventions.

record.name: GAD
record.evidence: "high immunoreactivity to the synthetic enzyme of the GABA mechanism, glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD)"
record.rationale: The source uses GAD for glutamic acid decarboxylase in general and names no isoform such as GAD65 or GAD67. The abbreviation covers more than one gene, Gad1 (GAD67) and Gad2 (GAD65). The 1983 paper reports immunoreactivity to an antiserum against the enzyme, which does not separate the isoforms. Per the skill's caution on families behind one abbreviation, it is NO_SINGLE_GENE (GENE_FAMILY). I did not run the lookup, because only GENE names go through Steps 2-3. The lookup would likely have returned a misleading single synonym match such as Uchl1.

record.name: SOM
record.evidence: "SOM+ interneurons selectively target the dendrites of BLA principal neurons"
record.rationale: The lookup returned AMBIGUOUS, with Sst and Grhl3 as the claimants. The evidence quote does not define SOM. The context is amygdala interneurons, and the title mentions low-threshold spiking interneurons. In neuroscience, SOM is the standard abbreviation for somatostatin, which marks this interneuron class. Grhl3 is a transcription factor and has no link to interneuron labelling. This call rests on field convention, not on the quote itself. The gene ID and symbol come from the lookup, which was run with the pinned gene-id tool because GENE_ID_BIN was not set.

record.name: ENK
record.evidence: "enkephalin-positive (ENK) neurons giving rise to the geniculo-geniculate tract innervating the contralateral IGL"
record.rationale: The paper defines ENK as enkephalin-positive. Enkephalin is encoded by proenkephalin (Penk). The lookup of 'ENK' returned Penk (NCBIGene:29237) as a UNIQUE_SYNONYM, and a direct lookup of 'Penk' gave the same ID as an EXACT_SYMBOL match in rat. The evidence is consistent with this. Enkephalin is derived only from Penk, so the name maps to one gene.

record.name: CRF
record.evidence: ".We then applied immunohistochemistry (IHC) to assess co-expression of CRF with our DREADD virus in dlBNST neurons"
record.rationale: The lookup of 'CRF' was AMBIGUOUS, with claimants C1ql1 (NCBIGene:23829) and Crh (NCBIGene:12918). The evidence does not define CRF. It describes IHC for CRF in BNST neurons, and the title is about BNST neurons and ethanol intake. In neuroscience, CRF is the standard abbreviation for corticotropin-releasing factor, and 'CRF neurons' in the BNST are a well-known population. C1ql1 lists CRF only as an obscure synonym. I chose Crh on field convention, not on a definition in the quote. A confirming lookup of 'Crh' returned EXACT_SYMBOL, NCBIGene:12918.

record.name: M2
record.evidence: "Trilaminar cells have a high level of somato-dendritic muscarinic M2 acetylcholine receptor" (PMID:32016558)
record.rationale: The evidence defines M2 as the muscarinic M2 acetylcholine receptor, which is the protein product of Chrm2. The lookup for the bare string 'M2' in mouse was AMBIGUOUS, with claimants Chrm2, Rasl2-9 and Rmst. Chrm2 is the only claimant that fits the evidence, and a follow-up lookup of 'Chrm2' gave an EXACT_SYMBOL hit (NCBIGene:243764). The taxon is Murinae and the evidence does not name the species, so I used mouse, the best-studied member. If the paper used rat, the ortholog would be rat Chrm2.

record.name: GABAA
record.rationale: GABAA receptors are a family of pentameric ligand-gated channels encoded by many subunit genes (Gabra1-6, Gabrb1-3, Gabrg1-3, Gabrd and others). The quote refers to 'GABAA receptors' generally and names no subunit. The 'extrasynaptic high-affinity' wording points to delta-containing receptors, but the source does not say which subunit, so no single gene can be assigned. Under Step 1 this is a family and skips the lookup. A lookup would likely return a single synonym match such as Gabrg1, which the skill's cautions warn against accepting.

record.name: OT
record.evidence: "unlike parvocellular CRF neurons that showed 83% co-expression with OT mRNA transcripts, none of the Type III CRF neurons tested co-expressed OT. Conversely, whereas 95% of Type III neurons expressed transcripts for OTR (18/19)..." (PMID:24009552)
record.rationale: The lookup returned a single synonym match, Oxt (oxytocin/neurophysin I prepropeptide), in rat, with no other claimants. The evidence fits it. OT is measured as mRNA transcripts in CRF neurons of the paraventricular hypothalamus, and it is paired with OTR, the oxytocin receptor. The paper does not spell out 'OT' as a name. The reading rests on the field convention that OT means oxytocin, and on the OT/OTR pairing in the quote.

record.name: TH
record.evidence: "In summary, TH neurons projecting to cortex vs. subcortical targets were enriched in distinct sets of clusters."
record.rationale: Here TH is the abbreviation for the thalamus, a brain region, and not tyrosine hydroxylase (Th). The passage is about 58 'thalamic neuronal cell clusters' of Epi-Retro-Seq projection neurons. It uses 'TH →SC', 'TH →VTA', 'TH →P' and 'TH →cortex' as source-to-target projection labels, and it links the RSP-projecting clusters to the anteroventral and anterodorsal thalamic nuclei. This is a Step 1 decision, so I did not run the gene lookup. A lookup would probably return Th, which is the wrong reading.

record.name: TH
record.evidence: "Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) staining of NE neurons in coronal slices."
record.rationale: The evidence defines TH as tyrosine hydroxylase, used to stain noradrenergic neurons in the mouse locus coeruleus. The lookup of 'TH' (case-insensitive symbol match, no other claimants) returned mouse Th, NCBIGene:21823, and that gene fits the evidence. The source writes the human-style symbol TH, and the official mouse symbol is Th.
